title: The Evolution of Software Development
description: Understand the transition from manual coding to AI agent orchestration and how your role as a developer is evolving.
learning_objectives: Contrast traditional manual coding with AI-assisted development workflows
Distinguish between AI Copilots (assistants) and AI Agents (autonomous executors)
Identify the shifting responsibilities of a developer from syntax writer to system orchestrator
prerequisites: Basic understanding of software development lifecycles

sections.heading: The Era of Manual Coding
sections.content_brief: Discuss the traditional workflow: searching documentation, writing boilerplate by hand, and manual debugging. Explain the cognitive load associated with syntax memorization and API discovery.

sections.heading: The Rise of AI Copilots
sections.content_brief: Explain the transition to 'autocomplete on steroids.' Focus on how LLM-powered assistants reduce friction by suggesting lines of code and implementing small functions based on comments.
sections.code_context: Comparing a manual function implementation versus an AI-suggested completion for a common utility task.

sections.heading: The Shift to AI Agents
sections.content_brief: Define the leap from Copilots (which wait for user input) to Agents (which can plan, execute, and iterate). Discuss how agents interact with filesystems, terminals, and browsers to complete end-to-end tasks.
sections.code_context: An example of a high-level agentic prompt that describes a feature request rather than a specific code snippet.

sections.heading: Redefining the Developer Role
sections.content_brief: Map out the new developer responsibilities: moving from 'writing' to 'reviewing,' 'architecting,' and 'verifying.' Emphasize the importance of critical thinking, security auditing, and system design over syntax fluency.

admonitions.content: While agents can write code autonomously, they lack business context and intuition. The developer's role shifts from 'how to write this' to 'what exactly should be built and why.'
Over-reliance on AI generation without rigorous review can lead to 'hallucinated' bugs or security vulnerabilities that are harder to debug than manually written code.
